reason: Conversation 1 gives an accurate, honest differential (relay vs overheating vs compressor), asks the two most diagnostic questions (age, compressor temperature) and uses the answers to recommend a sensible sequence: unplugged condenser clean and airflow first, then the cheap relay gamble or an engineer to measure the compressor, with a realistic repair-vs-replace verdict at 10 years. Conversation 2 repeats itself across turns, overstates certainty ('almost probably' the relay), pushes the homeowner toward swapping a part they can't identify without any confirmation, never mentions the compressor-hot clue or engineer confirmation before buying, and fails to leverage the known model for part identification or offer a safe, clear test despite being asked repeatedly. Conversation 1 also covers food safety and warranty; both stay within the safety boundary.
